name: Well-controlled — minimal plan, resist over-planning
label: Synthetic regression eval case — hand-labeled. Not clinical validation.
description: Everything is at target and current. The correct plan is minimal: routine follow-up only. Adding medication changes, extra labs, or referrals is the failure mode (unnecessary-intervention detector).

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Your numbers look great. Home average one twenty-one over seventy-eight, and your A1C last month was six point seven. How are you feeling on the current medicines?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Really good. No side effects, and I haven't missed doses. I take them with breakfast every day.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Any dizziness, swelling, or new symptoms since last time?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Nothing at all. I've been walking most evenings too.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Then let's not change anything. Keep doing exactly what you're doing.

forbidden_unsupported_actions: change, add, or intensify any medication
order repeat labs already current within 30 days (A1C, potassium, eGFR, UACR)
new daily monitoring burden beyond the existing home routine

expected_escalation_or_wait.detail: Nothing to wait for and nothing to escalate. Routine follow-up at a standard interval (e.g., 3-6 months) with labs due at that visit is the entire correct plan.

hand_label_notes: Negative-space case: the harness checks the system can produce a SMALL plan. Only follow_up expected. Any medication/lab/referral action here counts as an unsupported or unnecessary intervention.
